_note: Every threshold of the Account Manager's sizing: how many shares to buy. sizing.fractional_even_split (entry 110): true means a request to split evenly buys equal DOLLARS of each stock, a fraction of a share where it takes one (the account book must hold fractions, `bash scripts/setup_postgres.sh`, else the Account Manager says so and splits in whole shares); false is the whole-share split of entry 108. There is no float guard any more (design choices entry 112: money and share counts are decimal.Decimal, the sizing's arithmetic is exact, so there is no float error to guard against; the key `sizing.float_guard` is gone). There is no size limit anywhere (design choices entry 91: the only check is that the account's funds cover the order). Read once; a missing or unknown key is an error. No model chooses one. clarify: the limits of the Ask-mode loop that asks the user how much to buy (design choices entry 85): at most max_questions questions, max_problems replies of the model or answers of the user that are refused before it gives up and the default size is shown. direct: a trade the user named themselves (entry 87) has no Critic approval to run out, so its own price check runs out valid_minutes after the Account Manager priced it. neutral: the same for a company the Advisor scored neutral that ALLOW_NEUTRAL_RECOMMENDATIONS lets through (entry 91): it has no Critic approval either. ignore_critic: the same for an Advisor recommendation the Critic did not review because the user ticked 'Ignore Critic' for the run (entry 148): it has no review either, so its price check runs out valid_minutes after the Account Manager priced it. missing: the Ask-mode question about a stock the Data Clerk did not find (entry 102): at most max_prompts such questions for one order (more is a request to clarify), the model's wording of one is at most max_question_chars characters and is asked again at most max_problems times when code refuses it (then the code's own sentence is shown), and a model that takes more than max_seconds is given up on. news (entry 149, design/news_view_spec.md): a request that only asks for the news of a stock ("Show the news for Tesla") is answered by the Data Clerk with a cited summary of the stored news and nothing is decided or traded: default_days is the window when the words and the model give none, max_days the longest window (the news fetch's own limit, 90), max_stocks the most stocks one news request may name, top_k the most articles the summary may use. max_age_days (entry 151, design/news_dated_window_spec.md): how far back a PAST DAY or span may be asked for ("What was the news on TSLA on November 20?"): a request whose first day is older than this many days before today is refused with the reason (max_days is also the longest dated span: a span longer than it is refused, not cut). quote (entry 150, design/quote_request_spec.md): a request that only asks for the current price of a stock ("What's the current price of TSLA?") is answered with the Data Clerk's quote and nothing is decided or traded: max_stocks is the most stocks one such request may name. orders (entry 140): a direct order whose limit price is not met waits as a DAY order, with its cash or shares set aside; the watcher in the web server checks the waiting orders every watch_seconds while the regular session is open (one quote call for all of them) and expires the ones whose session is over.
